purpose: A place to review suggestions, compare the paths each one offers against stated criteria, see what is blocked until a question is answered, and record a choice before anything is implemented. Nothing on this page changes the site by itself.

criteria.name: Legality and terms
criteria.question: Does the path stay inside the NBA's terms, Dutch gambling law and the data licences this project actually holds?
scale: 0 = would break a stated term or law as read
1 = unresolved, and the risk is on the owner
2 = inside the terms as read, with a residual risk named
3 = no identified objection on the sources read

criteria.name: Effect on decision quality
criteria.question: Does the path make a decision on this site better informed, or does it only make the site prettier?
scale: 3 = closes a gap that currently blocks a decision

criteria.name: Evidence available now
criteria.question: Can the path be carried out and checked with the sources this repository already holds, without new data or new permissions?
scale: 1 = needs a licensed feed or a legal opinion

criteria.name: Reversibility
criteria.question: If the owner dislikes the result, how cheaply can it be undone?

criteria.name: Contribution to the brief
criteria.question: How directly does it serve the owner's stated goal — originated lines, gated strategies, injury-driven rotation analysis, 3-day picks?

questions.question: What NBA content may be reproduced or published on a public site?
questions.known: Terms of Use s.1 restricts reproduction and public or commercial use without written permission. s.9 requires attribution, limits NBA Statistics to news or private non-commercial use, bars use in connection with any gambling activity, and bars comprehensive statistics databases without consent. This site reproduces an injury snapshot and schedule rows with attribution and links. Page last updated July 13, 2026.

questions.question: Can picks or betting recommendations be published to people in the Netherlands?
questions.known: Not determined. Art. 1 of the Wet op de kansspelen prohibits promoting participation in unlicensed gambling (see S12). Ksa states that without a licence an operator may not advertise at all, and that online sports betting needs an Art. 31a licence (S10, S11). This is not legal advice. No picks are published.
questions.missing: Dutch counsel opinion on whether picks, tips or analysis count as promotion
questions.how_to_discover: Obtain a written legal opinion. Until then, picks.html publishes blank cells and no picks

questions.missing: Counsel opinion on prizes and rewards
questions.how_to_discover: Obtain counsel opinion before any reward is described on the site

questions.question: Do you want the site to publish model-derived numbers that no official source confirms?
questions.known: The brief requires a source link on every row and blanks for anything not confirmable from an official source. Model outputs (spread, total, probability) are by definition ours, not official.

questions.question: What sample size and decision rule should gate a strategy as deployable?
questions.known: The gate set in this repository proposes n >= 100 out-of-sample games, raw p < 0.05, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 0.05 and a stable split-half direction. Thresholds are proposals, not owner decisions.
questions.missing: Owner approval of the thresholds, the loss function and the prize structure of the leaderboard.
questions.how_to_discover: Approve or amend the gate thresholds on the Strategies page; the leaderboard ranks by them.

questions.question: What does winning the leaderboard actually pay?
questions.known: The board ranks rules by a composite skill score and assigns reward tiers T1-T5 with a stake allocation (full unit / quarter unit / paper only / none). No money is attached.
questions.missing: Whether this is a prize contest, a pool, or internal scoring. Dutch rules treat these differently (Q-LEG-01, Q-LEG-02).
questions.how_to_discover: Decide the competition format first; the reward schedule follows from it.

questions.question: Who may add a strategy to the board, and how is it registered before it is scored?
questions.known: Any rule can be scored. Nothing stops a rule being written after the results are known, which is how a backtest invents an edge.
questions.missing: A pre-registration step: rule text, selection predicate and freeze date hashed before the first forecast is graded (gate G10 idea).
questions.how_to_discover: Approve a pre-registration rule and add it as a gate; until then treat every strategy here as retrospective.

questions.question: Is 100 graded out-of-sample forecasts the right minimum sample?
questions.known: Gate G3 uses n >= 100. With ~1,230 NBA games a season and rules that fire on a subset, 100 takes one to three seasons for the narrower rules.
questions.missing: The cost of waiting versus the cost of acting on noise. 100 is a convention, not a measurement.
questions.how_to_discover: Approve, raise or lower the number; the board re-scores automatically.

questions.question: May per-player game logs be captured and stored?
questions.known: Without them every player-level correlation is blank and no prop combo can be priced. Four combos on the board are blocked on this alone.
questions.missing: Storage, volume (~4,000 rows a season) and the reproduction terms in NBA s.1 and s.9.
questions.how_to_discover: Decide, then capture nba.com/stats/players/boxscores by date and re-run the lab.

questions.question: Should a detected bias against our own line be reported as an edge or as a model defect?
questions.known: Our margin model is unbiased (+0.01 points) but the totals model runs about 1.5 points hot. A rule that fades our own high totals therefore 'wins' against us.
questions.missing: Nothing external. Beating our own line is not beating a market.
questions.how_to_discover: Confirm the policy: a bias found against our own line is published as a model defect to fix, never as a betting edge.

questions.status: Partly answered by this round — needs a standing rule
questions.known: The brief asks for a suggestions section reviewed before any change, and also for the session to finish without manual input. This round resolved the tension by changing presentation only (a header badge, a re-price column, a leading funded-state line, one corrected table) and flagging those edits here, so the owner can reverse any of them as a set. No published number, no model output and no other session's tree was touched.

questions.question: Should a line that is priced before a filing deadline be re-priced automatically when the deadline passes, or held and marked stale?
questions.known: Known: the deadline for every team-game in the window is computable from the official rule and the official schedule, and scripts/report_availability.py already publishes it per game. Five of tonight's ten team-sides settle at 1 p.m. local today. Known: nothing re-pulls today.
questions.missing: Missing: whether an automatic re-price is wanted (it changes published numbers without a human in the loop) or whether the site should only show the age and let the reader decide.
questions.how_to_discover: Pick one: (a) re-pull and re-price on the deadline, (b) re-pull and publish as a shadow line next to the original, (c) leave as it is. (b) keeps an audit trail and is what the leaderboard would need anyway to score strategies fairly.

questions.question: Should there be one canonical result log for the whole repository?

questions.missing: Missing: a decision on which log is canonical, and whether the older trees are re-cut or labelled as dated snapshots.

questions.question: Is a venue time-zone table acceptable as an input?
questions.known: Known: the official rule states deadlines in LOCAL time; the official schedule prints tip times in ET. The offset between the two is not printed on any official page this project reads, so 're-price at 13:00 local' is shown as local and the ET equivalent is left blank.
questions.missing: Missing: permission to use a published time-zone reference (which would let the site print '1:00 p.m. local = 2:00 p.m. ET' and rank tonight's games by when each becomes priceable).
questions.how_to_discover: Either accept an external time-zone source and record it in the source register, or keep the blank and accept that the ordering, not the clock time, is what the site can promise.

questions.question: Does a game with an unresolved side belong in a parlay at all?
questions.known: Known: same-game parlays on the site are priced with a measured dependence ratio of 0.942 whose interval includes 1.0, so independence is not established; and 22 of 27 games have no usable availability. The flag that said every game was a valid leg is now derived from availability instead of being a literal.
questions.missing: Missing: the owner's policy on leg eligibility — zero legs is a defensible answer for tonight, but not for a whole slate.
questions.how_to_discover: Choose a rule: exclude any leg whose team has not filed; or allow pre-deadline legs and mark them; or gate legs on strategy funding instead of availability. The first is the strictest and the easiest to defend.

questions.question: How should a Probable or Available-with-injury row affect a line?
questions.known: Known: the engine counts Out and Doubtful as absences and treats Questionable as 'listed but not counted'; Probable and Available (9 rows on the 11/14 slate, e.g. Caleb Martin with a thumb splint, Nolan Traore with a calf) currently have no effect at all.
questions.missing: Missing: a measured minute-donation model for game-time decisions, which needs per-player game logs this repository does not have.
questions.how_to_discover: Either state on the page that Probable/Available rows are ignored and why, or capture player game logs and measure how minutes actually shift for splint/mask cases. The first costs nothing.

how_to_use: Start with the blocked column. A suggestion whose dependency question is still open cannot be implemented correctly yet, whatever path is chosen.

For each ready suggestion, read the paths against the five criteria. The criteria are scored 0-3 with the meaning of each score written out, so a disagreement is about the path and not about the scale.
Where this session has a recommendation, the reason is stated. Where it does not, the row says so — an unscored row is a request for a reviewer, not a silent ranking.
Record the choice in COORDINATION.md against the suggestion ID. The site is rebuilt from the registers, so the record and the page cannot drift apart.
